perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- He is Ethan Mohamud, a Black man and plumber; Gary Guo is his close, long-time friend since middle school and an Asian doctor.
- He directly noticed Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep, and he worried about Gary’s health.
- He invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat and told him his health mattered. Gary declined, saying he had too much hospital work.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding talk about work. Ethan suspected the overworking involved more than professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school and Gary could tell him anything without judgment. Gary replied that it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- Gary then told Ethan about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy.
- Ethan offered to help Gary prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in, saw Gary making efforts and progress, felt hopeful and proud, and told Gary he was available to talk. Gary reported feeling better, less overwhelmed, and having had time for a movie.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing on his own, felt satisfied and happy, and decided to step back while telling Gary he was only a call away. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.
